findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` so it is never used
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers only consults predicate methods named `include_<attribute>?`. The method is defined as `include_website_name` (no question mark), so it is dead code and `website_name` is unconditionally serialized — e.g. it is emitted as `"website_name": null` for every user with no website, and, more importantly, it bypasses the intended guard entirely. Rename it to `include_website_name?` (and ideally base it on `website_name.present?`).

findings.title: `website_name` is not listed in `untrusted_attributes`, leaking TL0 websites to anonymous users
findings.body: `:website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109) so that a trust-level-0 user's website is hidden from anonymous visitors (anti-spam / SEO protection). The new `:website_name` attribute was added to `attributes` but not to `untrusted_attributes` and has no working inclusion guard, so the host (and now even the full path) of a TL0 user's website is serialized for anonymous requests, and `user.hbs` renders it (`{{#if model.website_name}}`). This re-exposes exactly the spam vector the untrusted_attributes list exists to block. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

findings.title: TL0/anonymous spec not updated for the new `website_name` attribute
findings.body: The `untrusted_attributes` list in the 'TL0 user seen as anonymous' context still only contains `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. The newly added `website_name` attribute is not asserted to be absent, which is why the regression that leaks a TL0 user's website host/path to anonymous visitors is not caught. Add `website_name` to that list (and a case asserting `website_name` is omitted when the profile website is blank).

findings.title: `"" << website_host` mutates a string literal instead of concatenating
findings.body: `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` uses destructive append on the literal `"."`. It happens to work today because each evaluation allocates a fresh literal, but it will raise `FrozenError` the moment the file gets a `# frozen_string_literal: true` magic comment (or runs under `--enable-frozen-string-literal`), breaking user serialization site-wide. Use `"." + website_host` or `".#{website_host}"`.

findings.title: Same-suffix heuristic treats unrelated hosts on shared domains as the same site
findings.body: The second branch considers two hosts related whenever they have the same number of labels (>2) and match after dropping the first label. For shared hosting suffixes this is wrong: with an instance on `forum.github.io`, an arbitrary user website `spammer.github.io` is judged to belong to the same organisation and the full URL path is rendered instead of only the host. Since the whole purpose of showing only the host is to avoid displaying attacker-controlled path text, this heuristic should use a public-suffix check or be restricted to an exact/parent-domain match.

findings.title: Only `path` is appended; query/fragment are dropped and `URI()` is re-parsed repeatedly
findings.body: `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` drops any query string or fragment, so `http://example.com/u?id=1` is displayed as `example.com/u`, which does not match the href the user clicks. It also re-parses the URI on every branch (up to twice per call) outside the `rescue nil` guard of line 138. Parse once into a local variable and build the display string from `path`, `query` and `fragment`.
